description: Detailed tier definitions for AIDIN maturity model

Foundational.generalDescription: Lacks most enabling factors; very limited adoption.

Infrastructure.general: Basic infrastructure is limited or non-existent. Connectivity is sparse, compute capacity is minimal, and energy access is unreliable.
Infrastructure.Connectivity: Limited or no broadband infrastructure. Mobile coverage is patchy. Most of the population lacks reliable internet access.
Infrastructure.Compute Capacity: Minimal data center infrastructure. Cloud services are largely unavailable or unaffordable.
Infrastructure.Energy: Unreliable electricity supply. Frequent outages limit digital infrastructure deployment.

Data.general: Data infrastructure is minimal. Limited data availability, no interoperability standards, and no digital public infrastructure.
Data.Availability: No open data portals. Government data is largely paper-based or inaccessible.
Data.Interoperability: No data standards in place. Systems operate in silos with no data exchange.
Data.Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI): No digital ID systems. No digital payment infrastructure. Citizens rely on paper-based systems.

Innovation Ecosystem.general: Very limited innovation capacity. Scarce talent, weak research institutions, and underdeveloped corporate structures.
Innovation Ecosystem.Talent: Few STEM graduates. Limited technical skills in the workforce. No specialized AI/ML training programs.
Innovation Ecosystem.Research Institutions: Minimal R&D investment. Universities lack research capacity in digital technologies.
Innovation Ecosystem.Corporate market structure: Few tech companies. No startup ecosystem. Traditional industries dominate.

Capital.general: Limited access to capital for digital transformation. Both public and private investment are minimal.
Capital.Public: No dedicated digital transformation budget. Limited public investment in digital infrastructure.
Capital.Private (Domestic vs. Foreign): Minimal private investment. No venture capital ecosystem. Foreign investment is rare.

Governance.general: No coherent digital strategy. Weak regulatory framework and limited enforcement capacity.
Governance.National Strategy: No national digital transformation strategy. Ad-hoc initiatives without coordination.
Governance.Regulatory Environment: Outdated or non-existent digital regulations. No data protection laws.
Governance.Enforcement: Weak regulatory enforcement. No dedicated digital governance institutions.

Digital Adoption.general: Very limited adoption of digital technologies in industry. No cyber-physical systems, minimal automation.
Digital Adoption.Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS): No integration of physical and digital systems. Manufacturing is largely manual.
Digital Adoption.Automation Maturity: Minimal automation. Most processes are manual with no digital integration.
Digital Adoption.Digital Twins: No digital twin implementations. No virtual modeling of physical systems.

AI Adoption.general: No meaningful AI adoption. Companies lack awareness and capacity for AI implementation.
AI Adoption.Operations Optimization: No AI-powered optimization. Operations rely on traditional methods.
AI Adoption.Smart Logistics: No smart logistics systems. Supply chains operate without AI assistance.

Digital Development.general: No digital product innovation. Companies focus on traditional products and services.
Digital Development.Servitisation: No shift to service-based business models. Products are sold as standalone items.
Digital Development.Digital Product Innovation: No digital products or services. Companies lack digital innovation capacity.

AI Development.general: No AI product development. No domestic AI capabilities or products.
AI Development.AI Product Innovation: No AI products developed domestically. Complete reliance on foreign AI solutions.

Emerging.generalDescription: Some enabling factors present; early signs of adoption.

Infrastructure.general: Basic infrastructure is developing. Some connectivity improvements, emerging compute capacity, and improving energy access.
Infrastructure.Connectivity: Growing broadband coverage, primarily in urban areas. Mobile networks expanding but gaps remain.
Infrastructure.Compute Capacity: Some data centers emerging. Cloud services becoming available but limited adoption.
Infrastructure.Energy: Improving electricity reliability. Some regions have stable power supply.

Data.general: Early data infrastructure development. Some data becoming available, initial interoperability efforts, and pilot DPI projects.
Data.Availability: Pilot open data portals. Some government data digitized but limited coverage.
Data.Interoperability: Initial data standards discussions. Some systems beginning to connect.
Data.Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI): Pilot digital ID programs. Early digital payment systems in development.

Innovation Ecosystem.general: Emerging innovation capacity. Growing talent pool, developing research institutions, and early corporate engagement.
Innovation Ecosystem.Talent: Increasing STEM graduates. Some technical training programs. Early AI/ML course offerings.
Innovation Ecosystem.Research Institutions: Growing R&D investment. Universities developing digital research programs.
Innovation Ecosystem.Corporate market structure: Emerging tech companies. Early startup ecosystem development.

Capital.general: Growing capital availability. Public investment increasing, private sector beginning to engage.
Capital.Public: Initial digital transformation budgets. Some public investment in key infrastructure.
Capital.Private (Domestic vs. Foreign): Early private investment. Some venture capital activity. Foreign investment increasing.

Governance.general: Developing digital strategy and regulatory framework. Some coordination and enforcement beginning.
Governance.National Strategy: Draft digital transformation strategies. Some coordination across ministries.
Governance.Regulatory Environment: New digital regulations being developed. Data protection laws in draft.
Governance.Enforcement: Regulatory institutions being established. Some enforcement capacity developing.

Digital Adoption.general: Early digital technology adoption. Some automation, pilot CPS projects, and initial digital transformation.
Digital Adoption.Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS): Pilot CPS implementations. Some integration of physical and digital systems.
Digital Adoption.Automation Maturity: Basic automation in some sectors. Early digital integration of processes.
Digital Adoption.Digital Twins: Pilot digital twin projects. Early virtual modeling initiatives.

AI Adoption.general: Early AI awareness and pilot projects. Some companies experimenting with AI.
AI Adoption.Operations Optimization: Pilot AI optimization projects. Some companies testing AI for operations.
AI Adoption.Smart Logistics: Early smart logistics pilots. Some AI-assisted supply chain initiatives.

Digital Development.general: Early digital product development. Some companies beginning digital innovation.
Digital Development.Servitisation: Early service-based models. Some companies adding digital services to products.
Digital Development.Digital Product Innovation: Initial digital products. Some companies developing digital services.

AI Development.general: Early AI development efforts. Some domestic AI capabilities emerging.
AI Development.AI Product Innovation: Pilot AI product development. Some domestic AI solutions in early stages.

Scaling.generalDescription: Strong enabling factors, but limited capacity in outcome areas.

Infrastructure.general: Solid infrastructure foundation. Good connectivity coverage, established compute capacity, and reliable energy supply.
Infrastructure.Connectivity: Broadband widely available in urban areas. Mobile networks cover most of population. Some rural gaps remain.
Infrastructure.Compute Capacity: Established data center infrastructure. Cloud services widely available and adopted.
Infrastructure.Energy: Reliable electricity supply in most areas. Some renewable energy integration.

Data.general: Well-developed data infrastructure. Good data availability, interoperability standards in place, and functional DPI.
Data.Availability: Operational open data portals. Significant government data available digitally.
Data.Interoperability: Data standards implemented. Good system integration and data exchange.
Data.Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI): Functional digital ID systems. Established digital payment infrastructure.

Innovation Ecosystem.general: Strong innovation capacity. Good talent pool, active research institutions, and vibrant corporate engagement.
Innovation Ecosystem.Talent: Strong STEM graduate pipeline. Good technical training. Established AI/ML programs.
Innovation Ecosystem.Research Institutions: Significant R&D investment. Active digital research. Good university-industry collaboration.
Innovation Ecosystem.Corporate market structure: Vibrant tech sector. Active startup ecosystem. Good corporate innovation.

Capital.general: Strong capital availability. Substantial public investment and active private sector participation.
Capital.Public: Dedicated digital transformation budgets. Significant public investment in infrastructure.
Capital.Private (Domestic vs. Foreign): Active private investment. Established venture capital. Good foreign investment.

Governance.general: Strong digital governance. Clear strategies, comprehensive regulations, and effective enforcement.
Governance.National Strategy: Comprehensive digital transformation strategies. Good cross-ministerial coordination.
Governance.Regulatory Environment: Comprehensive digital regulations. Strong data protection framework.
Governance.Enforcement: Effective regulatory institutions. Good enforcement capacity and compliance.

Digital Adoption.general: Moderate digital adoption. Some sectors well-digitized, but adoption is uneven across industries.
Digital Adoption.Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS): CPS implemented in some sectors. Good integration in key industries.
Digital Adoption.Automation Maturity: Moderate automation levels. Digital integration in many processes.
Digital Adoption.Digital Twins: Digital twins used in some industries. Good virtual modeling capabilities.

AI Adoption.general: Moderate AI adoption. Some companies using AI effectively, but adoption is not widespread.
AI Adoption.Operations Optimization: AI optimization in some companies. Good results but limited scale.
AI Adoption.Smart Logistics: Smart logistics in some supply chains. AI assistance improving efficiency.

Digital Development.general: Moderate digital product development. Some successful digital products, but innovation is limited.
Digital Development.Servitisation: Service-based models in some sectors. Companies adding value through digital services.
Digital Development.Digital Product Innovation: Some successful digital products. Good innovation in certain areas.

AI Development.general: Moderate AI development. Some domestic AI products, but capabilities are still developing.
AI Development.AI Product Innovation: Some domestic AI products. Good capabilities but limited scale and scope.

Frontier.generalDescription: Advanced ecosystems with widespread use and export capacity.

Infrastructure.general: World-class infrastructure. Universal connectivity, advanced compute capacity, and sustainable energy systems.
Infrastructure.Connectivity: Universal broadband access. Advanced mobile networks including 5G. High-speed connectivity everywhere.
Infrastructure.Compute Capacity: Advanced data center infrastructure. Widespread cloud adoption. Edge computing deployment.
Infrastructure.Energy: Reliable, sustainable energy supply. High renewable energy share. Smart grid infrastructure.

Data.general: Advanced data infrastructure. Comprehensive data availability, seamless interoperability, and mature DPI.
Data.Availability: Comprehensive open data ecosystem. Extensive government data available. High data quality.
Data.Interoperability: Seamless data exchange. Advanced standards. Full system integration.
Data.Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI): Mature digital ID systems. Advanced digital payment infrastructure. Comprehensive DPI.

Innovation Ecosystem.general: World-leading innovation capacity. Exceptional talent, top research institutions, and dynamic corporate structures.
Innovation Ecosystem.Talent: Exceptional STEM talent. World-class technical skills. Advanced AI/ML expertise.
Innovation Ecosystem.Research Institutions: High R&D investment. Leading digital research. Strong international collaboration.
Innovation Ecosystem.Corporate market structure: World-class tech sector. Vibrant startup ecosystem. Global innovation leaders.

Capital.general: Abundant capital availability. Strong public investment and highly active private sector.
Capital.Public: Substantial digital transformation budgets. Strategic public investment. Long-term funding.
Capital.Private (Domestic vs. Foreign): Highly active private investment. Mature venture capital. Strong foreign investment.

Governance.general: Exemplary digital governance. Visionary strategies, cutting-edge regulations, and world-class enforcement.
Governance.National Strategy: Visionary digital transformation strategies. Excellent coordination. Long-term vision.
Governance.Regulatory Environment: Cutting-edge digital regulations. Leading data protection. Adaptive regulatory framework.
Governance.Enforcement: World-class regulatory institutions. Excellent enforcement. High compliance rates.

Digital Adoption.general: Widespread digital adoption. Advanced CPS, high automation maturity, and extensive digital twin use.
Digital Adoption.Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS): Widespread CPS implementation. Advanced integration across industries.
Digital Adoption.Automation Maturity: High automation levels. Advanced digital integration. Smart manufacturing.
Digital Adoption.Digital Twins: Extensive digital twin use. Advanced virtual modeling. Industry-wide adoption.

AI Adoption.general: Widespread AI adoption. Companies using AI effectively across operations and logistics.
AI Adoption.Operations Optimization: Widespread AI optimization. Advanced AI-powered operations. High efficiency gains.
AI Adoption.Smart Logistics: Advanced smart logistics. AI-powered supply chains. High efficiency and optimization.

Digital Development.general: Strong digital product development. Successful digital products and services, strong innovation capacity.
Digital Development.Servitisation: Widespread service-based models. Companies thriving through digital services.
Digital Development.Digital Product Innovation: Strong digital product innovation. Successful digital products. Export capacity.

AI Development.general: Strong AI development. Domestic AI products competing globally. Export capacity.
AI Development.AI Product Innovation: Strong domestic AI products. Global competitiveness. Export of AI solutions.
